narrative: Material PL1__M6700059 shows moderate demand variability (CV=0.858) across 137 working-day observations from March 2025 to March 2026, with ~94% non-zero days indicating near-continuous consumption. Lead times are stable (CV=0.292) around a mean of ~1.5 working days, with one extreme outlier at 19.17 days that was winsorised. The (r,Q) continuous-review policy was selected: it batches replenishments at the EOQ-derived quantity (capped at storage capacity) and buffers demand uncertainty via a 1,031-unit safety stock, reducing total annual cost by 76.5% vs the SAP MOQ-only baseline.
warnings: Extreme lead-time outlier detected at 19.17 days (observation 103) — winsorised at 99th percentile (5.02 days) for policy calculations.
Storage capacity constraint is binding: safety_stock (1031) + order_quantity (5057) = 6088 == max_storage_units (6088.852). Order quantity was capped from unconstrained EOQ-based value.
SAP safety stock is 0 — current ERP configuration provides no buffer against demand/lead-time variability at 95% service level.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is near-continuous (94% non-zero days) with moderate variability and stable lead times — ideal conditions for a continuous-review (r,Q) policy. EOQ balances ordering and holding costs; safety stock is set via the normal-approximation formula at z=1.645 for 95% service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity binds tightly: the recommended policy uses 6,088 of 6,088.85 available units. Any upward demand shock or lead-time extension cannot be absorbed without exceeding storage. A 1-2% demand increase would require either expanded storage or a reduced order quantity — at the cost of more frequent replenishments.
